question: After the player defeats the Tiger Vanguard (虎先锋), what is the first line the Headless One (无头人) sings?
reference_answer: Gold and iron striking stone are entirely powerless; the Great Sage Tianpeng is bullied by the tiger.

db_evidence.notes: The correct first line ('金铁击石全无力，大圣天蓬遭虎欺', matching the reference translation) is visible on-screen for the whole 18025-18033s window (verified by extracting logical-time frames directly), but the memory DB's textual layer does not surface it cleanly: topic_facts row 00000306/00013029 timestamped at 18030 (the 30-sec caption boundary all rollouts anchored on) instead records a LATER subtitle pair ('铜刀对我手不痛，石棍似你不似你' / '小施主 筋骨轻奇 正相应着 铜头铁壁'), and no textual row captures the true first line verbatim. So text-only retrieval (semantic_search/run_sql over episodes/topic_facts/semantic_triples) cannot recover the answer; only a correctly time-windowed clip_qa call can, and even then the archaic second clause is prone to OCR-style misreading by the visual sub-agent. Additionally, the DB contains a second, distinct 'defeats 虎先锋' event around snapshot_s=16080 that is a genuine source of time-window confusion between the two boss-defeat moments.

root_causes: All rollouts anchored their clip_qa window start at the 30-sec caption boundary (18030) rather than the true clue start (18025), leaving the exact first-vs-second-line boundary to chance in the visual sub-agent's internal frame sampling.
Two rollouts (0, 4) had their clip_qa sampling land just past 18033 and transcribe the SECOND sung line, submitting it as if it were the first -> scored 0.

One rollout (2) confused the true final Tiger Vanguard defeat (~18000-18030s) with an earlier, differently-timestamped 'defeats 虎先锋' DB event (~16080s) and pursued the wrong window entirely, submitting unrelated spoken dialogue -> scored 0.

Two rollouts (1, 3) landed on frames within the correct clue interval and recovered the correct first clause verbatim, but both independently mistranscribed the archaic second clause (天庭逞虎威 instead of 天蓬遭虎欺), a font/blur-driven visual misread rather than a retrieval failure -> partial credit (2) each.

The memory DB's topic_facts summarization for this 30-sec clip omits the true first sung line altogether and instead records the subsequent line, so text-only retrieval paths could never have found the correct answer without visual verification.
what_worked: Both rollouts that scored non-zero used clip_qa with a window that (by chance) sampled frames inside the true clue interval and correctly identified/transcribed the first (easier) clause of the line.
Rollout 1's second, tighter frame-by-frame clip_qa re-check refined a spurious character (removed an incorrect 王) though it did not fix the deeper mistranscription.
transferable_lessons: For 'first line/first thing said after event X' questions, extend the clip_qa window to start a few seconds BEFORE the nearest 30-sec DB caption boundary, since the DB's caption bucketing can straddle the true event onset and omit it from the textual layer entirely.

When memory-triples/topic_facts show the SAME named event (e.g. 'defeats 虎先锋') at more than one timestamp, treat that as ambiguity requiring disambiguation (e.g. checking which one directly precedes a 'victory overlay'/'boss dissolves' marker) rather than picking one and committing to it.

For archaic/poetic on-screen subtitles, request a second independent clip_qa pass or ask the visual sub-agent to double-check each clause separately, since blur-prone classical Chinese text is systematically misread even when the correct frame is found.

Do not trust a single clip_qa evidence_times_s value as proof of 'the first occurrence' -- cross-check it against the clue_interval / total_intervals bounds when those are known, or against DB timestamps, before submitting.
open_questions: Whether the judge would have granted full credit if the second clause had been transcribed correctly but with 大圣 kept before 天蓬 in a slightly different order -- i.e. how much exact-wording strictness the judge applies to this recall-type question.

Why the visual sub-agent's frame sampling within the identical clip_qa window (18030-18060) diverged between rollouts landing on the first vs. second sung line -- this looks like nondeterministic internal frame selection by the sub-agent rather than a difference in the calling agent's instructions.
